prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Project asset for glenpadua.com, docs/art-style.md revision illustrated-world-v1. Generate ONE isolated transparent sprite composition. Reference1 beach is the primary illustration/identity reference; reference2 lake is CLOTHING ONLY (yellow/ivory vertical striped short-sleeve button shirt, dark shorts, tan sneakers); reference3 city is a seated character proportions reference. Match the simple warm lightly textured adventure-game illustration with restrained outlines, NOT pixel art, NOT realistic, NOT glossy 3D. Glen sits comfortably directly on the sand beneath a cream-and-muted-sage beach umbrella with a slender wooden pole behind him on viewer-left. Open small dark grey laptop rests naturally on his thighs; left hand rests at keyboard, right hand holds a short amber cold-drink tumbler beside his right knee (viewer-left). Tousled dark brown hair, sunglasses, tan skin, yellow and ivory vertically striped shirt, charcoal shorts. Both legs relaxed forward, slightly bent, clearly grounded. His anatomical LEFT leg (viewer-right) has a charcoal prosthetic socket and slim grey metal lower leg ending in a tan shoe; biological right leg is viewer-left. Never mirror. Keep face similar to approved beach/city character, head no more than one-third seated body height. Umbrella casts gentle shade over him; small soft ground-contact shadow only. Entire umbrella canopy, pole, character, feet, laptop and drink must fit comfortably inside square canvas with ~6% transparent margins, no cropping. Umbrella upper third, seated character lower half. No beach background, horizon, sky, sun, extra props, chair, football, text or logos. True transparent background; no checkerboard baked into pixels. Calm tidy complete silhouette, suitable for display at 230px wide.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target is this transparent 1280x1280 seated beach character sprite. Preserve EXACT canvas size, transparency, pixel registration, umbrella, pole, entire head location and expression, hair/sunglasses, shirt, laptop, left hand on keyboard, hips, both legs/feet, prosthesis, ground shadow and sand. Change ONLY his anatomical RIGHT arm/hand on viewer-left and the amber drinking glass it holds. He is now taking a sip: right elbow naturally bends, right hand lifts the SAME glass to his lips, rim touching mouth. Keep glass upright with slight tilt toward mouth, coherent wrist and grip, elbow/upper arm still joins the same shirt sleeve. The previous lowered glass and hand MUST be removed; naturally fill the small newly uncovered shirt/sand area. One arm, one hand, one glass only. Head must NOT move or tilt, laptop does not move. His anatomical LEFT leg remains prosthetic viewer-right. Same illustration rendering and outline weight. No extra fingers, no morphing, no new props, no scenery, no words. Output one complete sprite, not a sheet, TRUE transparent background.

Use case: precise-object-edit, hand-drawn animation in-betweens. Reference1 is resting pose, reference2 is sipping endpoint. Make a TWO COLUMN, ONE ROW sprite sheet, 2560x1280 pixels, each exact1280x1280 cell. Each cell is the complete original umbrella/seated Glen composition at the EXACT original position and scale; don't shrink or recenter. True transparent background. Cell1: only anatomical RIGHT arm (viewer-left) and drinking glass move halfway from resting knee position to chest, glass center about(510,835) in its cell, elbow bends naturally. Cell2: that same hand and glass are closer to the lips, glass center about(545,765), almost sipping. Keep original LEFT hand on keyboard unchanged in both frames. Copy umbrella, pole, head, hair, sunglasses, face, laptop, yellow/ivory striped shirt outside moving sleeve, charcoal shorts, relaxed legs with LEFT prosthesis viewer-right, shoes, sand contact patch EXACTLY unchanged from reference1. No second drink left by knee. Only shoulder/elbow/forearm/wrist articulate naturally, no stretching. Same small adventure-game illustration per docs/art-style.md illustrated-world-v1. No text, no grid lines, no borders, no extra props. The complete original sprite should occupy precisely the same coordinates inside each cell so these are stable registered animation frames.
